newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses ignore Tokyo woes, dollar firmer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses ignore Tokyo woes, dollar firmer.

text.p: Major European stock exchanges opened higher on Monday, taking heart from the Dow's continued record-breaking exploits and ignoring another overnight plunge in Tokyo.
The Japanese bloodletting did weaken the yen, however, and in the Far East the dollar was pushed to a 46-month high of 117.90 yen, though it fell back slightly in early Europe.

In Tokyo the key Nikkei average fell 3.37 percent, reflecting disappointment with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's failure to offer new economic initiatives in a closely-watched policy speech in parliament.
Against the mark, the dollar was also firm, as speculation increased of a possible German interest rate cut, though it was slightly off its overnight 31-month high of 1.6243 marks.
The mark, meanwhile, weakened against other European currencies, hitting a 31-month low against the lira and continuing to slide against the Norwegian crown.
In London, Europe's busiest bourse, dealers said shortages of stock were continuing to drive the market higher and another record peak looked well within reach.
"It would be no surprise to see another record today," one trader said. "There is plenty of cash coming into the market and that should keep driving it on today."
The blue chip FTSE index ended last week at a record close of 4,207.7, up 151.1 points or 3.7 percent over the week.
Despite its opening, the FTSE had fallen back somewhat into negative territory by 1000 GMT but dealers said bid rumours could well re-ignite the market.
Dealers said Wall Street's continued strength boosted stocks at the open, but some warned that the British market could soon have to stop for breath after its precipitous climb.
"We've come up an awfully long way awfully quickly," one said. "Nothing goes up in a straight line forever although the market is doing its absolute best to prove that it can."
On Friday the U.S. Dow had scored another record close, driven up 67.73 points to 6,833.1 by strong earnings news, a stable interest rate picture and sheer momentum.

In Frankfurt German shares also started higher in early electronic trade and opened half a percent up in floor business, boosted by the ever-strengthening dollar, which is good for German exports, and the firm close on Wall Street.
It was a similar story in Paris, were French stocks opened at historic highs, buoyed by the strong performance of the dollar and bond markets.
Dealers said the dollar had a firm tone in the European morning, even though it was off it highs against the mark and yen, and it was expected to continue to be robust.

"It will be a continuation of two themes. The U.S. economy is growing well and it's a question of when, rather than whether, the Fed will raise rates," said IBJ International chief analyst Keith Edmonds.
"On the other side of the interest rate equation, the groundwork is being laid for a German interest rate cut," Edmonds said.

Analysts said the dollar's rise was likely to be held in check by a partial holiday in the U.S. for Martin Luther King Day. U.S. stock exchanges and the New York Mercantile Exchange will operate normally.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was trading at 117.70 yen and 1.6230 marks compared with late Friday's European levels of 117.26 yen and 1.6135 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
London FTSE 100 index was down 4 points at 4203.7.
The German Dax index was up 15.47 at 3016.84.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 3.38 at 2428.48.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was trading in Europe at around $355.00 compared with a $355.15 close in London on Friday.
